Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Real feature request from the owner: a "Recently Updated" row on the NxLabs mod store, and they asked whether mods "have recent updates" tracked at all.

## The real gap (confirmed by reading the schema)
`GameMod` has `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` (Prisma auto-field — updates whenever OUR db row is touched, e.g. during a bulk re-import, NOT when the mod itself actually shipped a new version upstream) and `verifiedAt` (when our own verify script last checked it). NEITHER reflects real upstream release recency. Building a "Recently Updated" row on `updatedAt` would be dishonest — it would show whatever we happened to last re-sync, not what's actually freshly updated by its real author.

## What to build
1. Add a new real field to `GameMod` in `prisma/schema.prisma`, e.g. `upstreamUpdatedAt DateTime?` — the REAL last-modified timestamp from each source's own API:
   - **Modrinth**: real `date_modified` field on the project (verify live via their API, don't assume the exact field name without checking).
   - **GitHub**: real `pushed_at` field on the repo (or the release's `published_at` if that's more meaningful for a mod that ships via releases — use judgment, document your choice).
   - **Thunderstore**: package version data has real date fields — check the live API response shape for the actual field name.
   - **Steam Workshop**: `time_updated` field from `GetPublishedFileDetails`.
   - If mod.io import has landed by the time you start (check `git log` for a mod.io commit), that source has a real `date_updated` field too — include it if present, but don't block on it if it hasn't landed yet.
2. Write a migration + backfill script (`scripts/backfill-upstream-updated.ts`, dry-run by default, idempotent) that populates this field for all currently-imported mods by re-querying each source's real API (batched/rate-limit-aware per source's known limits from earlier research this session — GitHub unauthenticated is 60/hr core, Modrinth 300/min, etc.).
3. Add `listRecentlyUpdatedMods(family?, take)` to `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, ordered by real `upstreamUpdatedAt desc`, filtering out nulls (mods without a real timestamp yet just don't appear — never fake a date).
4. Add a "Recently Updated" row to BOTH the marketing `/mods` homepage and the per-family `/mods/games/[family]` page, using the existing `ModCard` component (same pattern as the just-built "Featured"/"Most downloaded" rails from `lib/mods-catalog.ts`'s `listFeaturedMods`/`listTopDownloadedMods` — read those and their usage in `app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx` and `app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx` first, match the same visual/structural pattern). Show a real relative-time label on the card or row (e.g. "Updated 3 days ago") if there's a sensible place to add it without a big card redesign — check if `ModCard` already has a slot for this kind of metadata; if not, a small addition is fine, but don't do a full card redesign (that's owned by other recent work).

## Answer the owner's actual question honestly in your report
"Do all of these updates have recent updates?" — report the REAL distribution once you backfill: how many mods have a real `upstreamUpdatedAt` within the last 30/90 days vs. older vs. null/unknown, broken down by source. Don't just say yes/no — give real numbers.

## CRITICAL process rule (still in force)
Multiple agents running their own `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` concurrently corrupted the build output earlier tonight and caused a real production outage. **Do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, poll every 30s until clear. Make your changes, run the backfill against the real DB (this needs no deploy itself, but the schema migration + new UI code does), verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`, commit and push to `main`, then STOP. I (the parent session) am batching commits and will deploy everything together myself.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (especially the recently-added `listFeaturedMods`/`listTopDownloadedMods`), and both target pages in full before editing.
- DB reads/writes only via `db` from `lib/db`, scripts under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` or a properly-named reusable script via `npx tsx`. NEVER print/construct a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string.
- A schema change needs `npx prisma migrate dev` or equivalent (check how this repo runs migrations — likely `prisma db push` given `deploy-staging.sh`'s "Applying database schema" step uses that pattern, check the actual scripts) — run it directly against the real dev/shared DB per this repo's existing convention (check `scripts/db-target-guard.ts` for how other scripts pick prod vs staging DB targets safely).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Commit and push to `main` (check `git log origin/main` before/after for concurrent pushes from sibling agents).

Report back: the real per-source distribution of upstream-update recency (the owner's actual question), confirmation the new row renders with real data on both pages, and confirmation you committed without deploying.
